title: Thursday, 10:40 p.m.
intro: The Playhouse after the show that never changes. The ghost light is on.

items.label: The Prompt Book
items.text: A thick book on the prompt desk. Page one, 1962. Margins crammed with pencil: CAST CHANGE. U/S. 'Seat them all.' The writing begins as a child's and grows up down the page.

items.label: Row W, Seat 9
items.text: One seat, reserved. A programme lies on it, with a name pencilled on the front, rubbed so many times it has gone soft. You can't read it.

items.label: Prop cabinet: a thousand keys
items.text: A pegboard of house keys, every one with a red ribbon tag. Every home in Little Mercy, tagged and hung.

items.label: The ghost light
items.text: A single bare bulb on a stand, left burning so the theatre is never dark. 'So whoever's in here never has to be alone.'

items.label: The pageant lamp
items.text: The big lamp, the real one, in a glass case. The glass has a crack. It matches the one in your closet.

items.label: Costume rail
items.text: Aprons, hats, one very ancient lamp-bearer's smock, your size. Someone has ironed it recently.

items.label: 1962 poster: THE RAISING
items.text: Same show, same cast list, every year. Only the nine-year-old is different.

items.label: The stage
items.text: Boards worn pale in a path from the Chapel door to the lake backdrop. Sixty-two years of the same walk.
